title: Require a mechanism, owner and measure for each active spec requirement
summary: Add mechanism, owner and measure to every active requirement in docs/spec.toml, enforce them in the spec test, make the Hestia sweep queue one deduplicated steward request per requirement lacking a mechanism (urgent for speed), and list such requirements in athena status.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require fmt, clippy -D warnings and tests passing.
The spec test and sweep enforce the rule rather than prose.
Fixture tests check queueing, idempotence and status listing.
Fields and docs are written for outside readers.
One change within the five named files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (default_checks, run_sweep, repeated_causes, root_cause_request building via crate::steward::StewardRequest), crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs (StewardRequest::new, queued_work) and crates/athena-core/src/status.rs, plus xtask/tests/spec.rs (serde Spec/Requirement with deny_unknown_fields, so new fields must be added to the struct). The sweep checks run in run_sweep over default_checks; the new check parses docs/spec.toml, dedups against open requests by citing the requirement id in request text (as addressing_request does), and needs no new record type under crates/, so check_record_file and AnyRecord are untouched.
Goal: make the spec enforce that each active requirement has a meeting mechanism; audience is Sri and the Hestia sweep and status readers.
The spec parser in athena-core is a small serde struct mirroring the xtask one, since xtask tests cannot be imported; athena-core likely already has the toml crate.

A failing measure is determined by a simple recorded measure check where feasible; otherwise only the missing or none mechanism triggers a request, and the measure check is limited to the field being present. Superseded or non-active requirements are exempt.
Mechanism text is filled from current code by the producer, which is judgment-heavy across 135 requirements.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: Grep of docs/spec.toml shows every active [[requirement]] (135 entries today) carries mechanism, owner and measure; where nothing meets one, mechanism is the literal "none". The measure names where it appears in athena status.
Run `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`: it passes on docs/spec.toml, and new in-memory negative cases fail an active requirement missing mechanism, owner or measure.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`: a fixture-spec test shows the sweep queues exactly one request for an active requirement whose mechanism is none, built via StewardRequest, and none on a second run while the first is open. A requirement about speed gets an urgent request (OP-23). A failing measure is also flagged.
Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`: a fixture test shows athena status lists active requirements with no mechanism, and lists none when all have one.
Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` (workspace): all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the mechanism, owner and measure fields, the sweep check and the status listing.
The requirement that Athena gets measurably faster and owns its acceleration records a mechanism (or none) and an owner, so it is visible, not omitted.

out_of_scope: Changing BRIEF.md or the source quotes in the spec
departures: Larger than reference: 135 requirements to fill from code plus three code areas and tests.
urgent_reason: Marked urgent by the request; it prevents a speed requirement from sitting two weeks without a mechanism.
hard_reason: Adds a Hestia sweep check that queues requests and a spec test gate, changing a rule that can hold work and the sweep pipeline.
